subject: Biotechnology
title: Quality Control in Biologics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Quality Control in Biologics usable.

hook.text: A single misfolded protein can kill — quality control in biologic manufacturing is a matter of life and death.

buildup.text: Mass spectrometry confirms the protein's exact mass and amino acid sequence — every batch is verified.

discovery.text: Glycan profiling ensures sugar modifications are consistent — even small changes affect drug safety and efficacy.

twist.text: Aggregation is the silent killer — clumped proteins trigger immune reactions. Size exclusion catches aggregates.

climax.text: Process analytical technology monitors quality in real time — catching problems during production, not after.

punchline.text: Test everything, trust nothing — QC keeps biologics safe.

quiz.question: Why is protein aggregation a safety concern in biologics?
options: Aggregated proteins are always inactive and waste money
Clumped proteins can trigger dangerous immune reactions in patients
Aggregation makes proteins too large to inject

details.summary: Biopharmaceutical quality control encompasses hundreds of tests ensuring product identity, purity, potency, sterility, and stability. Unlike simple chemical drugs, biologics require testing for protein aggregation, glycosylation patterns, host cell impurities, and residual viral particles.
details.whyItMatters: Quality failures in biologics can cause severe immune reactions or loss of efficacy. Rigorous quality control protects patients and maintains regulatory compliance, while also representing a significant component of overall drug manufacturing costs.
takeaways: Biologics undergo hundreds of quality tests throughout manufacturing
Each batch must demonstrate consistent protein structure and activity
Quality control accounts for a substantial portion of biologic production costs

faq.question: Why is quality control harder for biologics than chemical drugs?
faq.answer: Chemical drugs have fixed molecular structures verifiable by simple analytical methods. Biologics are complex proteins with multiple structural levels, variable sugar modifications, and potential for aggregation. Living cell manufacturing introduces variability that chemical synthesis avoids.

faq.question: What happens if a biologic batch fails quality testing?
faq.answer: Failed batches are destroyed entirely, potentially costing millions of dollars in lost product and manufacturing time. Root cause investigation is mandatory. Repeat failures may require manufacturing process changes and additional regulatory review. Patient supply can be disrupted.
